affected_components.role: Rejects dead_rootmount before accepting a lower mount and busying the supplied lower mount.
Wraps lower VFS dispatch through mp->mnt_lower in vfs_busy/vfs_unbusy after the fix.

code_slices.fixed: The patch first rejects lowermp == dead_rootmount and wraps each shown lower VFS call with vfs_busy(mp), conditional dispatch on success, and vfs_unbusy(mp).
code_slices.surrounding_context: The post-fix layerfs source retains the guarded VFS_FHTOVP dispatch before constructing a layer vnode.
code_slices.vulnerable: The patch's removed lines show direct VFS_QUOTACTL, VFS_STATVFS, VFS_VGET, and VFS_FHTOVP calls on mp->mnt_lower without a surrounding busy hold.

sources.concept: local layered-filesystem mount activity during lower-layer forced unmount

impact.attacker_capability: An actor able to perform the required local mount and layered-filesystem activity may trigger the recorded deadfs panic; required privileges, filesystem configuration, and timing are not established by the retained excerpt.
impact.security_effect: Kernel denial of service through panic.

causal_trace.summary: Mount activity reaches the kernel mount syscall path; the case report attributes the crash to syz-executor but the retained material does not include the complete reproducer or exact setup sequence.

Before the fix, layerfs operations directly passed mp->mnt_lower to lower VFS operations without a vfs_busy/vfs_unbusy lifetime hold; the fix describes this as walking down the stack during forced unmount of the lower layer.
Lower-mount setup had no explicit rejection for dead_rootmount; the patch adds an ENOENT return when the candidate lower mount equals dead_rootmount.

A lower filesystem operation can be dispatched through the layer after the relevant mount lifecycle has reached deadfs; the observed failing stack calls dead_panic through VFS_SUSPENDCTL and vfs_suspend during mount processing.
dead_panic produces the observed kernel panic string "dead fs operation used," terminating normal kernel operation and yielding an availability failure.

failure.operation: dead_panic reached through VFS_SUSPENDCTL during vfs_suspend in mount processing

primary_invariant.statement: A layered filesystem may install only a non-dead lower mount and must keep the relevant filesystem busy while a layer VFS operation walks through mp->mnt_lower.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Removed pre-fix calls directly dispatched VFS_QUOTACTL, VFS_STATVFS, VFS_VGET, and VFS_FHTOVP using mp->mnt_lower, while the patch adds busy/unbusy guards and a dead_rootmount rejection.

quality.review_notes: Crash evidence and a maintainer-authored two-file fix support the lifecycle mechanism and panic impact. The full syzbot reproducer, exact mount/filesystem setup, privilege requirements, race timing, pre-fix full source, and a post-fix run result are absent from the retained evidence. The crash stack does not itself name a layerfs dispatch function; attribution to mnt_lower traversal relies on the linked fix.

remediation.invariant_restored: Lower mounts cannot be installed as dead_rootmount, and layerfs lower-stack VFS calls are executed only while vfs_busy succeeds and until vfs_unbusy is performed.
mitigation_classes: hold filesystem busy lifetime protection around layered lower-stack VFS dispatch

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The retained crash record demonstrates mount-syscall activity, but does not provide the complete setup, concurrency schedule, privileges, or filesystem topology.
data_structure_invariants: mp->mnt_lower must not be dead_rootmount when installed as a layer lower mount.
A lower-stack VFS traversal originating in layerfs requires a successful filesystem-busy hold for its duration.
state_context.state_machine: A lower mount may undergo forced unmount and reach dead_rootmount/deadfs while a layered filesystem still attempts lower-stack VFS traversal.
